    // The surface rebuilt from its mapped UV-corner points. A Planar face
    // decays to Bilinear (a warped plane is no longer a plane); a Bilinear
    // face maps its four corners.
    Deform(s: BrepSurface, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): BrepSurface =>
        match (s) {
            Planar(patch) => Bilinear(BilinearPatch(
                mapping(patch.Eval(UvCoordinate(0.0, 0.0))),
                mapping(patch.Eval(UvCoordinate(1.0, 0.0))),
                mapping(patch.Eval(UvCoordinate(0.0, 1.0))),
                mapping(patch.Eval(UvCoordinate(1.0, 1.0)))));
            Bilinear(patch) => Bilinear(BilinearPatch(
                mapping(patch.P00), mapping(patch.P10),
                mapping(patch.P01), mapping(patch.P11)));
        };

    // The edge with its curve deformed; the vertex indices are unchanged.
    Deform(e: BrepEdge, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): BrepEdge
        => (e.Start, e.End, e.Curve.Deform(mapping));

    // The face with its surface deformed; the loop topology is unchanged.
    Deform(f: BrepFace, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): BrepFace
        => (f.Surface.Deform(mapping), f.Loops);

    // The IDeformable3D obligation: the whole shell with vertices, edge curves,
    // and face surfaces moved through the same mapping — topology unchanged.
    Deform(b: Brep3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): Brep3D
        => (
            b.Vertices.Map(mapping),
            b.Edges.Map(e => e.Deform(mapping)),
            b.Faces.Map(f => f.Deform(mapping)));

    //==
    // # BREP primitive shells
    //
    // Literal watertight shells built directly from the brep.types.plato vocabulary.
    // v1 ships the axis-aligned box; the cylinder-with-seam and prism of the C#
    // sketch wait on the Arc / QuadGrid sum cases. Conversion FROM the generative
    // solids (`ExtrudedSolid.ToBrep`, ...) is explicitly out of scope here and
    // tracked separately.

    // A straight shell edge between two vertices of a position array, carrying
    // the line segment through those positions as its curve.
    StraightEdge(vertices: Array<Point3D>, start: Integer, end: Integer): BrepEdge
        => (
            VertexIndex(start),
            VertexIndex(end),
            Line(Line3D(vertices[start], vertices[end])));

    // A forward citation of edge e in a face boundary loop.
    ForwardUse(e: Integer): BrepEdgeUse
        => (UndirectedEdgeIndex(e), EdgeOrientation.Forward);

    // A reversed citation of edge e in a face boundary loop.
    ReversedUse(e: Integer): BrepEdgeUse
        => (UndirectedEdgeIndex(e), EdgeOrientation.Reversed);

    // The bilinear face surface over a quad a-b-c-d wound counter-clockwise
    // seen from outside: U runs a to b, V runs a to d, so du x dv points out.
    QuadPatch(a: Point3D, b: Point3D, c: Point3D, d: Point3D): BrepSurface
        => Bilinear(BilinearPatch(a, b, d, c));

    // The axis-aligned box shell: base on the XY plane, centered in X and Y,
    // V=8, E=12, F=6, Euler characteristic 2. Every edge is cited once
    // forward and once reversed, so the result is watertight by construction.
    Box(width: Number, depth: Number, height: Number): Brep3D
    {
        var x = width / 2.0;
        var y = depth / 2.0;
        var p0 = Point3D(-x, -y, 0.0);
        var p1 = Point3D(x, -y, 0.0);
        var p2 = Point3D(-x, y, 0.0);
        var p3 = Point3D(x, y, 0.0);
        var p4 = Point3D(-x, -y, height);
        var p5 = Point3D(x, -y, height);
        var p6 = Point3D(-x, y, height);
        var p7 = Point3D(x, y, height);
        var vertices = [p0, p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6, p7];
        var edges = [
            StraightEdge(vertices, 0, 2),
            StraightEdge(vertices, 2, 3),
            StraightEdge(vertices, 3, 1),
            StraightEdge(vertices, 1, 0),
            StraightEdge(vertices, 4, 5),
            StraightEdge(vertices, 5, 7),
            StraightEdge(vertices, 7, 6),
            StraightEdge(vertices, 6, 4),
            StraightEdge(vertices, 3, 7),
            StraightEdge(vertices, 5, 1),
            StraightEdge(vertices, 0, 4),
            StraightEdge(vertices, 6, 2)];
        var faces = [
            // Bottom (0-2-3-1, seen from below).
            BrepFace(QuadPatch(p0, p2, p3, p1),
                [BrepLoop([ForwardUse(0), ForwardUse(1), ForwardUse(2), ForwardUse(3)])]),
            // Top (4-5-7-6).
            BrepFace(QuadPatch(p4, p5, p7, p6),
                [BrepLoop([ForwardUse(4), ForwardUse(5), ForwardUse(6), ForwardUse(7)])]),
            // +X side (1-3-7-5).
            BrepFace(QuadPatch(p1, p3, p7, p5),
                [BrepLoop([ReversedUse(2), ForwardUse(8), ReversedUse(5), ForwardUse(9)])]),
            // -X side (0-4-6-2).
            BrepFace(QuadPatch(p0, p4, p6, p2),
                [BrepLoop([ForwardUse(10), ReversedUse(7), ForwardUse(11), ReversedUse(0)])]),
            // +Y side (2-6-7-3).
            BrepFace(QuadPatch(p2, p6, p7, p3),
                [BrepLoop([ReversedUse(11), ReversedUse(6), ReversedUse(8), ReversedUse(1)])]),
            // -Y side (0-1-5-4).
            BrepFace(QuadPatch(p0, p1, p5, p4),
                [BrepLoop([ReversedUse(3), ReversedUse(9), ReversedUse(4), ReversedUse(10)])])];
        return (vertices, edges, faces);
    }

    //==
    // # BREP tessellation
    //
    // The exact-to-discrete seam for BREP shells: sampling each face's surface
    // over the full unit UV square into an indexed triangle mesh. Like the C#
    // sketch it ports, v1 tessellates the FULL UV grid and ignores loop clipping
    // — exact for the faceted Planar / Bilinear cases whose loops span the whole
    // patch (Box does), approximate once trimming loops arrive. Triangles wind
    // counter-clockwise seen from outside when the surface follows the outward
    // du x dv convention (brep.types.plato).

    // One triangle of a full-grid tessellation over a cols x cols vertex
    // lattice (cols = resolution + 1): triangles 2*cell and 2*cell + 1 split
    // grid cell `k / 2` along its low-UV-to-high-UV diagonal.
    GridTriangleFace(k: Integer, cols: Integer): TriangleFace
    {
        var cell = k / 2;
        var col = cell % (cols - 1);
        var row = cell / (cols - 1);
        var a = row * cols + col;
        var b = a + 1;
        var c = a + cols + 1;
        var d = a + cols;
        return k % 2 == 0
            ? (VertexIndex(a), VertexIndex(b), VertexIndex(c))
            : (VertexIndex(a), VertexIndex(c), VertexIndex(d));
    }

    // The face's surface sampled on a (resolution + 1)^2 UV grid, two
    // triangles per cell. Precondition: resolution >= 1. Vertices are not
    // welded across faces; per-shell welding is future work.
    Tessellate(f: BrepFace, resolution: Integer): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var cols = resolution + 1;
        var positions = MapRange(cols * cols, i =>
            f.Surface.Eval(UvCoordinate(
                (i % cols).ToNumber / resolution.ToNumber,
                (i / cols).ToNumber / resolution.ToNumber)));
        var faces = MapRange(2 * resolution * resolution, k =>
            GridTriangleFace(k, cols));
        return (positions, faces);
    }
